inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, consolidated cash flow note 29(a) share-based compensation add-back RMB45,968k; no net-share-settlement taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in every period)
inputs.share_count_basis: 131,619,251 shares in issue at 30 Jun 2026 plus 0.83m dilutive options/RSUs (H1 2026 interim note 12 diluted-EPS adjustment) = 132.5m fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Option-exercise proceeds (RMB15.9m FY2025) are immaterial and ignored.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1727 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16). Cross-checked USDHKD 7.8483 / USDCNY 6.6754 = 1.1757 and 1/HKDCNY 0.8518 = 1.174 on the same date; no dual listing exists for a parity check. All flows and per-share values are built in CNY and converted once at this rate; refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate, so re-check it on any later price-only refresh.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10y CGB ~1.8% risk-free, ~6.5% China equity risk premium plus ~1pp small-cap/HK-liquidity premium, beta ~1.1 for a consumer-discretionary roll-out -> cost of equity ~10%. Net cash (no structural borrowings beyond a RMB200m revolving facility), so WACC = cost of equity = 10.0%. Same rate in all three scenarios: cyclicality, the subsidy war and franchisor dependency are charged in the flows and the weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full lease cash (principal RMB370.2m + interest RMB74.0m FY2025, both in FINANCING on the IFRS-16 cash flow statement, so reported OCF/FCF exclude them) is deducted inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path (8.25% of revenue FY2025, 8.57% H1 2026). Lease liabilities (RMB2,031m at 30 Jun 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (RMB320.2m FY2025 = 5.95% of revenue, from the MD&A D&A line), so the lease is charged once. ebitda_margin_path is post-IFRS-16, pre-SBC EBITDA (reported EBITDA + SBC add-back = RMB1,029.4m = 19.1% FY2025).
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interests; 100% owned operating subsidiaries.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, QSR master franchisee), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (non-US operating company) with the adaptations file applied for currency (CNY flows / HKD quote), heavy IFRS-16 leases (treatment B), and interest income stripped against net cash held in the bridge. Owner FCF FY2025 = 386.9 reported FCF - 370.2 lease principal - 74.0 lease interest - 46.0 SBC - 17.3 interest income = RMB-120.6m: the company is reinvesting all operating cash into ~300-350 new stores a year (capex 9.4% of revenue vs maintenance of ~5%), so the valuation rests entirely on the terminal owner-FCF margin once rollout decelerates. House and street bases differ only by SBC (~0.5-0.85% of revenue), so the band is narrow. Cash tax rate ramps from ~57% of modelled EBIT in FY2025 (profitable PRC entities taxed at 25% while new-city entities run start-up losses that cannot be grouped) to 28% by year 8. Buybacks: none; flat count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for in cash. Price is a regular Friday close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Year-1 revenue growth from store rollout: ~350 net new stores on 1,315 (+27% units) less negative same-store sales (-4.8% H1 2026) and lower-tier-city mix dilution; H1 FY2026 actual +20.8%. Equity CAGR is not used because the 2023 IPO and convertible conversion inflated book value.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: History is FY2022-FY2025 only (listed March 2023), so no 5-year CAGRs. Equity 3yr CAGR 47.9% exceeds revenue 38.6% because of IPO proceeds and convertible-share conversion, not retained earnings. EPS CAGR is not computable (FY2022 loss). Owner-FCF CAGR is not meaningful: owner FCF has been negative every year once lease cash (RMB444m FY2025) and SBC are charged, versus reported FCF growing 64%/yr from a 2022 base -- the reported series is flattered by IFRS-16 classification of lease payments in financing.
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF 3yr CAGR of 64% is an artefact: it excludes lease cash that scales one-for-one with the store base. On an owner basis the company has not yet generated positive free cash flow in any year.

base.narrative: Store count reaches ~3,000 around FY2031 (guidance) and ~3,400 by FY2035; revenue growth decelerates from 19% to 3.5%. Lease-adjusted pre-SBC EBITDA margin troughs at 9.7% in FY2026 (full-year subsidy-war effect) and recovers to 13.0% by FY2033 as new-city cohorts mature and corporate overhead is leveraged. Capex falls from 9% to 5.5% of revenue (maintenance plus ~3% unit growth). Cash tax normalises from 50% to 28%.

bull.narrative: Platform subsidies recede through 2027, average transaction price recovers and SSSG returns to low-single-digit positive; 350-400 openings a year carry the network past 3,000 by FY2030 and ~4,000 by FY2035. Lease-adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 14.9%, in line with mature Domino's master franchisees.

bear.narrative: Third-party platforms become the permanent channel: ATP stays down, SSSG stays negative into 2027, and lower-tier-city paybacks stretch, so management slows openings to ~250 a year from FY2027 and the network stalls near 2,300-2,500 stores. Lease-adjusted EBITDA margin never recovers past 10%; owner FCF margin matures at ~2.7%.

scenario_narratives.base: The two axes are (1) how long the JD/Meituan/Ele.me delivery subsidy war keeps average transaction price down 9-10% and store-level margin at 12.5% (H1 2026, from 14.5% in FY2024), and (2) whether the ~350-stores-a-year rollout into non-Tier-1 cities keeps earning 12-15 month cash paybacks as SSSG in new cities runs -9% to -13% off record opening weeks. Base assumes the subsidy intensity fades over 2026-27 but platform intermediation is permanent, so margin recovery is slow (lease-adjusted EBITDA 9.7% -> 13.0% over eight years) while the rollout hits the 3,000-store target on schedule. All value is terminal: owner FCF is negative in FY2026 and only turns meaningfully positive from FY2029 as capex intensity falls.
scenario_narratives.bull: Subsidies normalise, DPC's own-channel/loyalty base (41.9m members) claws back order share, ATP recovers and SSSG turns positive; new-city cohorts mature into the margin profile Tier-1 cities already show; openings stay at 350-400 a year and the network heads toward the 5,000 long-term ambition. Mature lease-adjusted EBITDA ~15%, in the range of Domino's Pizza Enterprises' better years.
scenario_narratives.bear: Platform disintermediation is structural: the platforms own the customer, ATP stays down, and the franchisee's thin store-level margin absorbs rider-cost and commission inflation. Lower-tier-city unit economics deteriorate, management throttles openings, operating leverage stalls at ~10% lease-adjusted EBITDA, and cash tax stays punitive because loss-making new entities cannot be grouped with profitable ones. The single-franchisor dependency means there is no portfolio pivot available.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: the margin-compression risk is live (H1 2026 SSSG -4.8%, ATP -9.6%, store-level margin 12.5%), owner FCF has never been positive, and the whole equity case is a terminal-margin recovery the company has not yet demonstrated. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things -- subsidy retreat, ATP recovery and sustained new-city paybacks -- to go right together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the business as a stream of owner cash flow after the full lease cost and SBC, in CNY at a CNY cost of equity, with net cash added once and interest income removed from the flows. Because the current owner FCF is negative by design (growth capex), the valuation is a judgment about the mature margin of a ~3,000-store Domino's China network and the probability that the delivery-platform shift permanently caps it; the scenario weights, not the discount rate, carry that risk.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal lease-adjusted EBITDA margin: each 1pp on the terminal margin moves base value by roughly 15-20% because owner FCF margin is only ~5%
Duration of the platform subsidy war and permanence of third-party-channel ATP dilution
New-city unit economics (cash payback) deteriorating as the rollout moves down the city tiers
Cash tax rate failing to normalise from ~50% toward 28% if new-entity losses persist
Master franchise agreement terms/renewal with Domino's Pizza Inc. (single-brand dependency)
CNY/HKD translation: per-share values are converted at a dated rate that price-only refreshes do not update
